title: MEDICATION ADMINISTRATION AND CALCULATION
knowledge: Explain the ten (10) rights of Medication Administration.
Discuss the rationale for completing a patient assessment prior to the administration of certain medication e.g. Digoxin
Explain the process of documenting new drug or contrast allergies and adverse drug even reactions.
Discuss how to carry out the document telephone and verbal orders.
Discuss High Alert Medications, the identification, location, labeling and storage relevant to area of practice.
Discuss the process for ordering, receiving and storage of all medications.
Explain the process of medication independent double checks as relevant to the area of practice.
Discuss the rationale to enforce policy regarding home medication in hospital.
Explain the role and responsibilities of the nurse when an adverse drug reaction occurs including the full document of the event.
State rationale for cleaning tablet cutter and clinical area after preparing IV medication e.g. antibiotics.
skills: Demonstrate the correct patient identification procedure as per policy.
Check patient's medical record for any documented drug or contrast allergies and risk prior to administering medications.
Demonstrate the different routes of Medication administration including the Ten (10) rights of Drug Administration.
Demonstrate at least one relevant drug calculation relevant to area of practice.
Complete documentation for Administration of Medication.
Complete documentation to record an adverse reaction.
attitude: Ability of Nurse to respond professionally and calmly if an adverse drug reaction occurs
Ability of the nurse to acknowledge limitations in knowledge and skills

Demonstrate ability to organize and facilitate a reflection session in and on practice after any learning opportunity is identified during the administration of medication and or the use of Drug Calculations and activate findings to improve practice response
To be approachable and open to answer patient and family question's
Ability to approach medical staff assertively and with sound knowledge base when there is any doubt with the prescription

title: MOVING AND HANDLING
knowledge: Explain the term biomechanics and its relevance in moving and handling.
Discuss why, how and when a risk assessment is performed.
Discuss the 5 main factors assessed prior to moving and handling patients.
Assess patient needs/ problems prior to moving a patient.
Discuss potential problems/ unexpected outcomes for the healthcare workers while moving a patient.
Discuss potential patient related problems/ unexpected outcomes while moving a patient.
State the nurse's role and responsibility when a problem is identified.
Discuss how to document the process of moving and handling a patient.
skills: Demonstrate correct body mechanics and ability to use appropriate and available equipment for various patient care moves.
Locate the correct equipment required to assist in a corresponding move.
Demonstrate preparing the patient prior to move.
Demonstrate how to Lead a successful move.
Discuss how to document the process of moving and handling a patient.
Carry out the nurse's role and responsibility when a problem is identified including the completion of the necessary reporting procedure and documentation required.
attitude: Ability of Nurse to respond professionally and calmly if a problem occurs before or during a patient move.
To be self-aware to limitation to knowledge and skills.
To be approachable and open to answer patients and family's questions.
Attentive to overall patient experience e.g. pain, anxiety and have ability to provide comfort and emotional support as needed.
Demonstrate ability to organize and facilitate a reflection session and on practice after a moving and handling learning opportunity occurs and activate findings to improve practice and response.
